main_text.l: ita scripsit. Mustelæ uentriculus Coriandro
fartus, & inueteratus comitialibus auxilia
turpotus. Item iecur asininum assatum in
cibis sumptum ieiuno stomacho. Aliud
croci, nardi, ana obolos duos; ueratri nigri
obolum unum, scammonij drachmas qua-
tuor, nitri drachmas duas, melle excipito,
& drachmas duas ex aqua mulsa bibendas
dato. Ciconiæ fimum ex aqua uel oxymeli
te propinato. Agarici obolos tres, peuceda
ni tantundem, coaguli phocæ, obolum u-
num, contrita hæc miscentur. Idé author
libr. de Materia medica scriptum reliquit,
coagulum phocæ epilepticis conferre. Est
autem phoca (teste Plinio) marinus vitulus.
Et libro tertio afferit Dioscorides, agaricū
facere ad morbum comitialem, sumptum
trium obolorum pondere. Eundem ait Ga-
lenus, libro Simplicium medicamentorum
sexto,
comitiali morbo obnoxios sanare.
Eodem in libro etiam inquit peucedanum
utiliter inungi, cum aceto & rosaceo epile-
pticorum capiti. Oribasius octauo libro ad
Euftatium tradit agaricum,
semen sesclis,
sphodilij radicem, & aristolochiæ rotundæ
radicem, ex aqua epotam, comitialibus p-
desse. Rutæ sylvestris semen cum aqua po-
tum

page.notes: Text is in a single column with small original sign beside "ueratri nigri" at the right margin (a printed reference mark/annotation, rendered as a blotted symbol). Damaged and faint at the margin; the sign was transcribed as a reference mark only. Upper text is partly cut at the top edge; "ita scripsit" is a fragment carried over from the previous page. Some words in the final lines are uncertain at the page-edge fold and the word "sesclis" and "epotam" are read with doubt; the last word "potum" is a line-end fragment. Heavy faint foliage show-through lower left is not transcribed.
